title: One pixel more than the memory ceiling allows
why: **The first illegal peak, not merely an illegal one.** The first record puts the document exactly on 640 MiB, so the 1 × 1 mask that follows overshoots by a single pixel — four bytes — and a consumer whose ceiling is wrong by any amount at all fails this case. It is nowhere near any other cap: two records, 67 megapixels, four artifacts of a few hundred bytes each. The refusal is `document-too-large`, the token every budget already refuses with — a memory ceiling is a budget, and giving it a token of its own would make the same class of refusal arrive under two names in two engines.
